title: Complementary Regulatory Dynamics: An Integrative Theory for Systems Biology and Dynamical Systems Medicine
content: Essential challenges persist in systems biology, especially data and model integration. These issues may explain the lack of a universally accepted framework in modern biology for organizing the dynamic behaviors of whole organisms and diseases across scales. This paper proposes Complementary Regulatory Dynamics (CRD) as an integrative theory for studying how complex adaptive systems generate necessary changes while preserving viable functions. CRD assigns functional activator and regulator roles to processes relative to a defined system boundary and focal outcome. The theory is organized around five provisional, testable principles. CRD may help integrate and enrich models from established theories, including nonlinear dynamical systems theory, homeostasis and allostasis, and resilience theory. CRD could provide a common logic for organizing complex biological networks. It may help identify causal variables and build explicit bridges linking multiple scales. As a falsifiable theory, it can improve experimental design and clinical testing by shifting from static biomarkers to dynamical biopatterns and time-sensitive approaches. In translational settings, this could help detect early-warning signals, transition-prone states, and intervention windows. Therapeutic strategies can focus on systems-based biotargets to restore dynamic balance. CRD theory may provide potentially unifying guidance for translating systems biology into dynamical systems medicine.
